title: Behavior of maximal functions in R^n for large n
version: Published 1983 article; public 11-page PDF copy downloaded from Tsinghua archive
actual_read: PDF pp. 1-2: title, introduction, centered maximal operator and definition of general bounded open convex symmetric B.
PDF pp. 2-6; print pp. 260-264: Theorem 1 statement and covering proof, including the covering lemma and its unspecified absolute constants.
PDF pp. 6-7; print pp. 264-266: Theorem 3 and heat-semigroup proof for the standard Euclidean ball only; checked to keep this result separate from cubes.

theorem_record.location: print p. 260 (PDF p. 2); proof on print pp. 261-264
theorem_record.operator: For bounded open convex symmetric B in R^n, M_B f(x)=sup_{r>0}|rB|^{-1} integral_{rB}|f(x-y)|dy, Lebesgue measure.
theorem_record.statement: There is an absolute c, independent of B and n>1, such that |{x:M_B f(x)>lambda}| <= c*n*log(n)*||f||_1/lambda for lambda>0.
theorem_record.conditions: Theorem states the weak-(1,1) estimate for the centered dilates of B; an open axis-parallel cube is an admissible B. The numeric value of c is not specified in the published statement.
theorem_record.finite_n6_use: Substitution gives only 6*c*log(6) with c unspecified; no comparison with 64 is justified from this source as published.

distinctions: Theorem 3 treats the standard Euclidean ball, not axis-parallel cubes, and gives c*n with unspecified c.
Theorem 2 is an Lp statement and is not a weak-(1,1) upper bound for this task.
No cube-specific finite-dimensional upper recurrence was read or established from this article.
